Dear Jaya didi,

Last month I told nobody how bad my marks were, and I kept thinking, this is who I am. Then at Diwali you and Anil bhaiya told me about the times each of you failed a paper: you a whole semester, him a board subject, and how you both laugh about it now. I hadn't known any of that. I've thought about it for weeks. I don't think it is the whole story any more. It's one stage. So I've set a smaller goal: clear the physics supplementary, then get back to steady work. And next time I feel this stuck, I'll call you early, not after weeks. Can we talk on Sunday?

Usha

qa.q: Who told Usha about failing papers at Diwali?
qa.a: Jaya didi and Anil bhaiya told Usha about the papers each had failed.

qa.q: What does Usha feel about the result now, compared with a month ago?
qa.a: Usha now sees the result as one stage and not the whole story, and feels steadier and more hopeful.

qa.a: Jaya is probably touched and glad to have been trusted, and pleased that sharing an old struggle helped.

You want to know if I'm still upset about the boards, Tushar? Not like before. Let me tell you why.

I'm Rekha. When I got 58 percent, I thought I'd let everyone down. I barely left my room for a week. Then, at my cousin's engagement in Indore, I ended up on the terrace with my older cousins, Pooja didi and Anshul bhaiya.

Pooja didi said she'd failed economics in Class 12 and had to take it again. She's an auditor now. Anshul bhaiya said he'd got a low rank in his entrance and went to a small college, then did a master's somewhere good.

They weren't lecturing. They were just telling stories. But I went home thinking, this is one stage, not the whole road.

A few weeks later I made one small goal: improve my maths basics before Class 12. And this time, when I got stuck in the first test, I asked for help in week one, not month three.

qa.q: What percentage did Rekha get in the boards?
How did Rekha feel in the week after the result?
qa.a: Rekha felt ashamed and low, thinking everyone had been let down, and barely left the room.

qa.q: What else could Rekha do to keep this new view of setbacks?
qa.a: Rekha could keep in touch with the cousins and share small wins with them, so the reminder that results are one stage stays close.

qa.q: How might Pooja didi have felt sharing her own failure on the terrace?
qa.a: She may have felt a bit exposed but glad to help, hoping her story would show Rekha that a setback does not decide a whole career.

grounding: A spoken account of a student who, after weeks and talks with older cousins, reframes a poor result as one stage, sets a smaller goal and seeks help earlier.

I'm Manjula, Pema's classmate in Gangtok. After our Class 10 results, Pema stopped coming to our evening study group. When I saw her in the market, she said, "What's the point? I'm the one who got 55."

A month later, her family went to Siliguri for a wedding, and she came back somehow different. In the canteen she told us her older cousin had failed his Class 12 once and now teaches at a college. Another cousin went to a smaller college and later got into a good master's.

I can't say what went on inside her. But she rejoined our group. She said she was aiming for a steady 70 in maths first, not topping. And when she didn't understand trigonometry in October, she went to Mr. Rai the very same week.

Before, she used to hide her tests. Now she shows them to us, even the bad ones.

qa.q: What mark did Pema say she got?
What might Pema have been feeling when she said "What's the point?" in the market?
qa.a: She probably felt discouraged and ashamed, seeing the result as proof she was failing.

qa.q: What else could Pema's study group do to support her?
qa.a: They could keep reviewing tests together openly, so asking for help early stays normal for everyone, not only for Pema.

qa.q: How did Pema's change look to Manjula?
qa.a: To Manjula it looked like a shift from hiding to openness, rejoining the group and showing even bad tests, though Manjula admits not knowing her inner thoughts.

grounding: An observer describes a student who, after talking with older cousins who also struggled, reframes a result as one stage, sets a smaller goal and seeks help earlier.
